claim: A voluntary partial payment that comes with written directions is applied as the taxpayer directs.
quote: A designated payment is a voluntary payment that the taxpayer has directed to be applied in a particular manner, i.e., to a specific period or kind of tax, or as a payment of tax or interest specifically, etc. Normally such direction will be followed by the IRS. ... Revenue Procedure 2002-26, section 3.02, provides that a voluntary partial payment accompanied by written directions as to its application will be applied pursuant to the taxpayer's written instructions.
source: IRM 5.1.2 Remittances, Form 809 and Designated Payments (5.1.2.9, revised 08-06-2025), via IRS search excerpt citing Rev. Proc. 2002-26 sec. 3.02
uncertainty: The quote comes from an IRS search excerpt of the IRM. I could not extract the Rev. Proc. 2002-26 text itself (IRB 2002-15 PDF did not parse).
suggestedSimplification: Let the player designate a payment to a specific tax year, or to tax rather than penalty or interest. If the player doesn't, the default order below applies.

claim: An undesignated payment goes to tax first, then penalty, then interest, oldest period first, in whatever order best serves the government.
quote: Apply available credits created by involuntary payments or by undesignated voluntary payments to satisfy outstanding balances in other tax periods in the order that best serves the interests of the government, considering the Collection Statute Expiration Date (CSED) for all outstanding liabilities. This will generally require application to the oldest tax, oldest penalty, and oldest interest, in that order until fully used.
uncertainty: This is the field-collection IRM. Within a single period, Rev. Proc. 2002-26 sec. 3.01 also orders tax, then penalty, then interest, but I did not read that text directly.
suggestedSimplification: Apply an undesignated payment to tax, then penalty, then interest, oldest year first.

claim: The penalty is 0.5% a month or part of a month, capped at 25%. It drops to 0.25% during an approved plan if the return was filed on time, and rises to 1% if the tax isn't paid within 10 days of a notice of intent to levy.
quote: 0.5% of the unpaid taxes for each month or part of a month the tax remains unpaid. ... The penalty won't exceed 25% of your unpaid taxes. ... 0.25% per month (or partial month) during your approved payment plan. ... 1% per month or partial month.
uncertainty: The 0.25% rate requires the return to have been filed on time.
suggestedSimplification: Charge 0.5% a month (0.25% on a plan if filed on time), capped at 25%.

claim: For individuals, interest is the federal short-term rate plus 3 points, compounded daily: 7% for Oct 1 to Dec 31, 2026.
quote: 7% for underpayments (taxes owed but not fully paid) ... compounded daily ... the federal short-term rate plus 3 percentage points
source: IRS newsroom, 'Interest rates remain the same for the fourth quarter of 2026', IR-2026-98
uncertainty: Low. The rate is reset quarterly.
suggestedSimplification: Use 7% a year, compounded daily, from the original due date until paid.

claim: The penalty is 5% of unpaid tax a month, capped at 25%, and reduced by the failure-to-pay penalty for the same month. Returns more than 60 days late pay a minimum of $525 (due after 12/31/2025) or 100% of the underpayment, whichever is less.
quote: The penalty is 5% of the tax due (less any tax paid on time and available credits) for each month or partial month the return is late. The penalty accrues up to a maximum of 25%. ... If the return is more than 60 days late, the minimum penalty is the amount listed below or 100% of the underpayment, whichever is less. [Return due date (without extension) After 12/31/2025: $525.00; 01/01/2025 to 12/31/2025: $510.00] ... the failure to file penalty is reduced by the amount of the failure to pay penalty (0.5% for each month).
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: Charge 4.5% for filing plus 0.5% for paying each month for 5 months (22.5% for filing at most). For returns over 60 days late, use the lesser of $525 or the tax due as the minimum.

claim: Paper filers amending a 1040-NR send Form 1040-X with page 1 identity only and attach a complete corrected 1040-NR marked 'Amended'. E-filers must complete Form 1040-X in full.
quote: If you are filing Form 1040-X on paper to amend Form 1040-NR, or to file the correct return, do the following ... Complete a new or corrected return (Form 1040, 1040-SR, 1040-NR, etc.). Across the top of the new or corrected return, write 'Amended.' Attach the new or corrected return to the back of Form 1040-X. ... If you are electronically filing Form 1040-X to amend Form 1040-NR, you must complete the Form 1040-X in its entirety.
source: Instructions for Form 1040-X (Rev. December 2025), 'Resident and nonresident aliens'
uncertainty: Low. The quote was paraphrased in part by the fetch tool, so check the wording before citing it.
suggestedSimplification: Treat it as one 'Amend' action for both 1040 and 1040-NR, and produce a corrected return labelled 'Amended'.

topic: A3 Amended return - time limit, interest
claim: A refund claim must be filed within 3 years of filing or 2 years of payment, whichever is later. The IRS adds interest to refunds. Additional tax owes interest from the original due date and a failure-to-pay penalty if not paid within 21 days of notice and demand.
quote: Generally, for a credit or refund, you must file Form 1040-X within 3 years (including extensions) after the date you filed your original return or within 2 years after the date you paid the tax, whichever is later. ... We will figure any interest and include it in your refund. ... The IRS will charge you interest on taxes not paid by their due date, even if you had an extension of time to file. ... If you don't pay the additional tax due on Form 1040-X within 21 calendar days from the date of notice and demand for payment ... the penalty is usually 1/2 of 1% of the unpaid amount for each month or part of a month the tax isn't paid.
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: Allow an amendment for 3 years after filing. A refund adds interest at the quarterly rate. Additional tax accrues interest from the original April due date.

claim: Processing usually takes 8 to 12 weeks and can take up to 16. A mailed amendment takes up to 3 weeks to appear in the tracking tool. A 1040-NR can be amended electronically for the current and two prior years.
quote: You should generally allow 8 to 12 weeks for your Form 1040-X to be processed. However, in some cases, processing could take up to 16 weeks. ... If you need to amend your Form 1040, 1040-SR, 1040-NR, 1040-SS, or (prior to 2023) 1040-PR for the current or two prior tax periods, you can amend these forms electronically ... It can take up to 3 weeks from the date you mail it to show up in our system.
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: Resolve an amendment 10 to 16 game-weeks after filing.

topic: A4 Substitute for Return - before assessment
claim: The automated SFR program (ASFR) assesses under IRC 6020(b). It sends a 30-day letter (Letter 2566), then a statutory notice of deficiency (90 days) under IRC 6212, then assesses by default. A return filed before assessment goes to processing in place of the SFR.
quote: The ASFR program assesses tax by authority of Internal Revenue Code (IRC) 6020(b) ... Statutory Notices of Deficiency are issued under authority of IRC 6212 ... At the conclusion of 30-Day Letter suspense period, if there is no/insufficient response ... ASFR generates a Statutory Notice of Deficiency (90-Day Letter) ... When ASFR returns (not reconsiderations) are received and the TC 971 AC 143 is present on IDRS, the ASFR system will be updated to the appropriate status and the returns will be shipped to the nearest submission processing site
source: IRM 5.18.1 Automated Substitute for Return (ASFR) Program (rev. 09-11-2025), 5.18.1.1.2, 5.18.1.2, 5.18.1.6.1, 5.18.1.6.6
uncertainty: CP3219A is the AUR (underreporter) notice of deficiency, not the SFR one. The CP3219A page doesn't address non-filers. In ASFR the 90-day letter is the Statutory Notice of Deficiency (Letter 3219 family). The fetch tool paraphrased part of the IRM, so check the wording before citing it.
suggestedSimplification: Not filing produces a 30-day letter, then a 90-day notice, then an assessment. Filing a real return before the assessment replaces the SFR.

claim: If the taxpayer neither responds nor petitions the Tax Court within the notice period, the IRS assesses the proposed tax and bills it, and interest accrues.
quote: If we don't hear from you and you don't file a petition, we'll assess the proposed changes and send you a bill. ... File your petition by the date listed on the notice. The Tax Court can't consider your case if you file the petition late.
uncertainty: This is the AUR-context notice. The default-assessment behavior is the same deficiency procedure.
suggestedSimplification: If the 90-day notice is ignored, assess the SFR amount (usually higher, with no deductions or credits) and add penalties and interest.

claim: After assessment, a taxpayer replaces an SFR by filing a signed original return, which is handled as an audit (SFR) reconsideration. Outcomes are full allowance (assessment abated), partial disallowance, or full disallowance.
quote: An audit reconsideration is the process the IRS uses to reevaluate the results of a prior audit where additional tax was assessed and remains unpaid, or a tax credit was reversed. ... when the taxpayer contests a substitute for return (SFR) determination by filing an original delinquent return ... The taxpayer must file a signed original return to request reconsideration of an SFR assessment.
uncertainty: The outcome categories (full allowance, partial disallowance, full disallowance) are a summary of the IRM, not a single quotation. The 'signed original return' sentence came from a search excerpt.
suggestedSimplification: Filing a late real return after an SFR assessment triggers a reconsideration. Abate the difference after 8 to 16 weeks. Late-filing penalties remain on the real tax.

claim: A short-term plan pays the balance within 180 days, requires owing under $100,000, and has a $0 setup fee. Penalties and interest keep accruing.
quote: Pay amount owed in 180 days or less ... You owe less than $100,000 in combined tax, penalties and interest. ... $0 setup fee ... Interest and some penalty charges continue to be added to the amount you owe until the balance is paid in full.
source: IRS, Payment plans; installment agreements (page updated 13-Aug-2026)
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: Offer a free plan of 180 days or less below $100k.

claim: The online long-term plan requires owing $50,000 or less with all returns filed. Setup fees are $29 online by direct debit, $107 by direct debit through phone, mail or in person, $69 online without direct debit, and $178 without direct debit through phone, mail or in person. Low-income filers (AGI at or below 250% of the poverty level) pay nothing by direct debit or $43, reimbursable, otherwise. The $22 the brief expected is outdated: the current fee is $29.
quote: You owe $50,000 or less in combined tax, penalties and interest, and filed all required returns. ... Apply online: $29 setup fee ... Apply by phone, mail, or in-person: $107 setup fee ... Apply online: $69 setup fee ... Apply by phone, mail, or in-person: $178 setup fee ... $43 setup fee which may be reimbursed if certain conditions are met
source: IRS, Payment plans; installment agreements (page updated 13-Aug-2026)
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: Use a $29 online direct-debit installment agreement for balances of $50k or less with all returns filed. The failure-to-pay penalty drops to 0.25% a month.

claim: A customer can cancel a switch up to 7 working days before the switch date, by contacting the new bank.
quote: You can cancel your switch up to seven working days before your switch date.
source: Current Account Switch Service (Pay.UK), FAQs / Common questions
uncertainty: Low. There is no separate 'cooling off' in CASS. The 14-day cooling-off on the new account contract (Consumer Credit / distance marketing) was not researched.
suggestedSimplification: A switch can be cancelled freely until 7 working days before the switch date and is locked after that.

topic: B6 UK CASS - timing and overdraft
claim: A switch takes 7 working days and the date can't fall on a weekend or bank holiday. An overdrawn customer must agree any overdraft with the new bank or repay the old one separately. CASS closes the old account and moves the balance.
quote: You'll need to allow 7 working days for the switch, and it can't be a weekend or a Bank Holiday. ... You will need to agree any overdraft facilities you require with your new bank or building society ... [they] may be able to provide lending facilities to help you pay off your existing overdraft ... your old bank will close your old account
source: CASS, The switching process; Common questions
uncertainty: Not found on CASS pages: what happens mechanically when an overdraft is left unresolved (the switch is refused, or the old account stays open). The FAQ fetch summarized that, if no agreement is reached, the customer must arrange repayment of the old overdraft separately. That is a paraphrase, not a verbatim quote.
suggestedSimplification: A switch from an overdrawn account requires the new bank to grant a covering overdraft or the debt to be cleared. Otherwise the switch fails before the switch date.

claim: Interest or charges on either account caused by a switching failure are refunded once the customer reports it to the new bank. Payment problems are corrected and the customer's credit rating is protected.
quote: This guarantees that any charges or interest incurred on your old or new account, as a result of a failure in the switching process will be refunded. ... If anything goes wrong, we will ensure that any charges or interest incurred on your old and/or new account as a result of the error will be refunded.
uncertainty: The credit-rating protection came from a search excerpt of the CASS site, not a fetched quote.
suggestedSimplification: If a switch error causes a fee or interest, refund it automatically.

claim: For switches since 16 Sep 2013, payments sent to the old account are redirected indefinitely, replacing the earlier 36 months. Third-party summaries say redirection lasts at least 3 years and continues until 13 months pass with no redirected payment.
quote: Customers who have switched their account to us since 16th September 2013 will benefit from a redirection service for an indefinite period of time, an extension to the previous 36 months offered.
uncertainty: The 3-year minimum and the 13-month rule come from search summaries (MoneySavingExpert/FCA), not an official verbatim quote. Each redirected payment also sends the payer the new details.
suggestedSimplification: Redirect payments to the old account to the new one indefinitely.

topic: B7 EU PAD Art. 10 - outstanding obligations
claim: The transferring provider closes the account on the date in the authorisation only if the consumer has no outstanding obligations. If obligations prevent closure, it must tell the consumer immediately. The consumer chooses which items to switch and the dates, at least 6 business days out.
quote: close the payment account on the date specified in the authorisation if the consumer has no outstanding obligations ... immediately inform the consumer where such outstanding obligations prevent the consumer's payment account from being closed.
uncertainty: This is point (e) of paragraph 4, not 10(5) as the brief guessed. Art. 10 has no explicit right for the consumer to cancel a switch, so customer cancellation is 'not found' in the directive. The switch of standing orders and direct debits can complete while the account stays open (a partial outcome).
suggestedSimplification: If the old EU account has debt, the switch still moves payments but the old account stays open with its debt, and the player is notified.

topic: B7 EU PAD Art. 13 - financial loss
claim: A provider that breaches Art. 10 must refund the consumer's resulting financial loss, including charges and interest, without delay.
quote: Member States shall ensure that any financial loss, including charges and interest, incurred by the consumer and resulting directly from the non-compliance of a payment service provider involved in the switching process with its obligations under Article 10 is refunded by that payment service provider without delay.
uncertainty: There is an exception for abnormal, unforeseeable circumstances.
suggestedSimplification: Treat this as the EU equivalent of the CASS Guarantee.

claim: Under ZKG §21 and §23(1) Nr. 5, the transferring provider closes the account on the authorised date once steps 1, 2 and 4 are done. The fetched ZKG text did not mention an outstanding-obligations exception or a consumer cancellation right.
quote: das bei ihm geführte Zahlungskonto schließen und einen verbleibenden positiven Saldo auf das beim empfangenden Zahlungsdienstleister geführte Zahlungskonto überweisen soll (§21(2) Nr. 4); ... zu dem in der Ermächtigung hierzu bestimmten Datum ... wenn die Schritte nach den Nummern 1, 2 und 4 vollzogen wurden (§23(1) Nr. 5)
uncertainty: Outstanding-obligations handling and cancellation: not found. The fetch tool may have summarized, and the full §23 wording was not verified verbatim.
suggestedSimplification: Use the PAD rule.

claim: Closing the old account is optional: the customer may mandate closure at a date of their choice. The process takes about 22 business days. For 13 months after closure the old bank must report transfers or cheques presented on the closed account.
quote: [vous pouvez] aussi mandater votre banque pour clôturer votre ancien compte, à la date que vous souhaitez
source: La finance pour tous (Banque de France-backed IEFP) - Le service de mobilité bancaire; CMF L312-1-7
uncertainty: The quote is a reconstruction from a translated fetch, so check the wording. Debit balance, cheques outstanding and mandate revocation: not found.
suggestedSimplification: Closure is an optional checkbox. The switch takes about 22 business days.

claim: The customer may close the old account or keep it open. The new account must be active within 10 working days of the agreed switching date.
quote: Your new account must be active within 10 working days of the agreed switching date. ... Decide whether to keep or close your old account
source: CCPC (Competition and Consumer Protection Commission), Switching your current account
uncertainty: The Central Bank Code PDF and S.I. 482/2016 could not be read (unparseable PDF and HTTP 403). Cancellation and outstanding-debt handling: not found.
suggestedSimplification: Ten working days, with an optional closure of the old account.

claim: Chase doesn't sell standalone personal loans. 'My Chase Loan' lends eligible cardmembers part of their existing credit card line, minimum $500, with no application or credit check.
quote: This feature is available to eligible cardmembers. ... Unlike traditional loans, with My Chase Loan there's no need for an application, credit check or a separate account to manage. ... The minimum amount you can request for My Chase Loan is $500.
uncertainty: 'Chase does not offer personal loans' came from a search summary, not a verbatim Chase quote.
suggestedSimplification: Chase gives no personal loan. A Chase cardholder can draw a fixed-rate loan against the card's credit line.

topic: C8 Bank of America - personal loans
claim: No Bank of America consumer personal-loan product was found. Its small-dollar product, Balance Assist, lends checking customers up to $500 for a flat $15 fee, repaid monthly over four months.
quote: This short-term low-cost loan for checking account customers can help you with unexpected expenses. ... Apply to borrow up to $500 ... $15 fee for opening a Balance Assist loan and there are no other interest or finance charges ... Repayment is made monthly over a period of four months
source: Bank of America, Banking Solutions (Balance Assist)
uncertainty: No BofA page explicitly says 'we don't offer personal loans', so that is 'not found' rather than confirmed. A search summary gave older terms ($5 fee, 90 days, account open at least 1 year). The fetched page says $15 and four months, so terms have changed. The account-tenure rule was not verified on the current page.
suggestedSimplification: BofA has no personal loan. Existing checking customers get a $100 to $500 advance for a $15 fee, repaid over 4 months.

claim: Wells Fargo lends only to existing customers of at least 12 months: $3,000 to $100,000 at 6.74% to 26.74% APR over 12 to 84 months.
quote: We only offer personal loans to existing Wells Fargo customers. ... Rates range from 6.74% to 26.74% APR.
uncertainty: The 12-month tenure, amounts and terms came from the same page but as a paraphrase.
suggestedSimplification: Only after 12 months as a Wells Fargo customer: a $3k to $100k loan.

claim: Wells Fargo Overdraft Protection links one savings and one credit account (credit card or line of credit) to checking, with no transfer fees. The overdraft fee is $35 per item.
quote: You can link up to two eligible Wells Fargo accounts (one savings and one credit account) ... We do not charge transfer fees or advance fees for Overdraft Protection. ... Our overdraft fee for items paid into overdraft is $35 per item.
uncertainty: Whether new personal lines of credit can still be opened: not found. The page refers only to an 'eligible linked Wells Fargo line of credit'.
suggestedSimplification: Overdraft protection pulls free from a linked WF savings account or card. Otherwise the fee is $35 per item.

topic: C8 Citi - personal loans and Checking Plus
claim: Citi lends to new customers ($2,000 to $30,000) and to existing customers (up to $50,000) at 10.24% to 18.49% APR over 12 to 60 months. Checking Plus was an overdraft line of credit, described in Citi's 2022 overdraft-fee elimination release.
quote: Personal Loans from $2,000 - 30,000 ... may be eligible for up to $50,000 ... Your APR may be as low as 10.24% or as high as 18.49% ... If approved, a Checking Plus(R) line of credit automatically transfers funds from your credit line to your checking account to cover your overdraft plus any fees.
source: Citi Personal Loans; Citigroup press release 2022-02-24
uncertainty: Whether Checking Plus is discontinued for new applicants: not found on an official page. Only forum reports exist.
suggestedSimplification: Citi lends to anyone ($30k new, $50k existing).

claim: Capital One now offers personal loans, through Discover after the merger. Older help pages said it didn't.
quote: Through our merger with Discover, Capital One now offers personal loans.
uncertainty: Discover loan eligibility (no existing-customer requirement, historically) was not verified.
suggestedSimplification: Capital One/Discover makes personal loans open to new customers.

claim: An arranged overdraft requires a current account at that bank, being 18 or over (Barclays also requires living in the UK), and is subject to status. HSBC charges 39.9% EAR above a £25 buffer (38.9% APR representative). Barclays charges 35.0% APR representative.
quote: You must be 18 or over to apply and live in the UK (Barclays) ... To apply for an arranged overdraft you'll need to be 18 or over. ... Credit is subject to status. ... 0% EAR (variable) on the first £25 ... 39.9% EAR (variable) above £25 (HSBC)
uncertainty: The current-account requirement is implicit (an overdraft attaches to that account). HSBC excludes its Basic Bank Account.
suggestedSimplification: An overdraft is only possible on an account you hold at that bank: 18+, subject to status, about 35 to 40% EAR.

topic: C9 UK personal loans - existing-customer rules
claim: Barclays requires a Barclays current account or Barclaycard. HSBC lends to non-customers (£1k to £30k, income at least £10k), with an instant decision for HSBC current-account holders and 2 to 5 days for others. NatWest lends up to £50k to existing customers and £35k to new ones. Lloyds lends £1k to £50k after 1 month with a Lloyds, Halifax or Bank of Scotland current account, and up to £35k otherwise.
quote: Have a Barclays current account or Barclaycard account (Barclays) ... If you've got an HSBC current account you can get an instant credit decision, while non-HSBC current account customers should get a credit decision in 2 to 5 working days. (HSBC) ... If you hold a Lloyds, Halifax or Bank of Scotland current account for at least 1 month, you could borrow between £1,000 and £50,000. If you aren't an existing Lloyds, Halifax or Bank of Scotland customer, you could still borrow up to £35,000. (Lloyds)
uncertainty: The Lloyds quote is from a search excerpt because the page returned an error when fetched. The NatWest £50k/£35k split is a paraphrase, and NatWest's 3-month account rule is stated for joint loans. Representative APRs: Barclays 7.05%, HSBC 6.8%, NatWest 7.2%.
suggestedSimplification: A UK loan at a bank where the player holds no account is either refused (Barclays) or capped lower (£35k), so existing customers get more.
